headline: Waymo launches $30/month Premier tier with priority pickups, but it's triple competitors' price
summary: Waymo Premier offers priority pickups and 10% rebates for $30 monthly, significantly more expensive than Uber One or Lyft Pink, which provide broader benefits for a third of the cost. The value proposition is questionable given Waymo's higher per-ride costs an
details: Alphabet-owned Waymo is rolling out "Waymo Premier," a new rewards program priced at $30 a month. Subscribers get priority pickups, a 10 percent in-app rebate for future rides, and up to five fee-free cancellations monthly.
This premium tier also offers early access to Waymo in new cities, essentially letting subscribers pay to beta test new coverage areas. However, this pricing stands in stark contrast to competitors.

Uber One costs $10 a month, offering discounts on hotels, car rentals, and food delivery, plus 6 percent ride credits. Lyft Pink, also $10 monthly, provides 5 percent off standard rides and free priority pickup.

The significant price difference raises questions about Waymo Premier's value, especially since Waymo rides are already generally more expensive than Uber or Lyft, according to a June 2025 report by Obi.

The premise of driverless taxis was to reduce costs by eliminating human labor. Yet, Waymo charges three times more for its premium subscription, on top of higher per-ride fees, for a system that still requires remote human intervention.

This comes amidst Waymo's recent safety issues, including a software recall for its entire fleet last month due to dangerous behavior during a flood. The company has faced scrutiny for incidents like driving through a police standoff.

While human-driven ride-shares have their own problems, the high cost of Waymo Premier combined with its operational challenges makes it a difficult sell. The value proposition for paying a premium for a service with known issues is unclear.

topic: Coinbase AI agent for crypto trading
headline_marked: [[Coinbase launches AI agent]] for crypto trading and premium research payments
headline: Coinbase launches AI agent for crypto trading and premium research payments
summary: The new agent can execute trades in crypto spot and derivatives markets, offer portfolio rebalancing, and pay for premium research using the open x402 payment protocol.
details: Coinbase has launched an AI agent capable of executing crypto trades and paying for premium research. This follows a trend of AI agents surpassing human internet traffic, with companies like Robinhood also introducing similar tools.

Users can integrate the agent directly with their main Coinbase account for trading, or choose a separate sandbox environment for testing. The agent leverages Coinbase Advanced, the platform for professional traders, which includes features like TradingView charts.

Capabilities include rebalancing portfolios, following investment theses, and providing one-time crypto trade advice. Currently, it supports crypto spot markets and derivatives, with future plans for equities and prediction markets.

The agent can utilize the open x402 payment protocol, co-launched by Coinbase with AWS, Anthropic, Circle, and Near. This allows it to pay for premium research data APIs and on-demand compute without requiring logins or subscriptions.

Coinbase has been actively investing in AI tools for years, having launched AgentKit in 2024 and an AI-powered assistant in December. The latest agent can also work within ChatGPT or Claude via its MCP server.

Lincoln Murr, Head of AI Product at Coinbase, stated the primary goal is to create agents that can transact. He noted Coinbase is unique in combining exchange access with a native payments protocol, aiming for a future internet accessed primarily through agents.

The rapid development in agentic payments, with recent investments from Visa in Replit and a deal with OpenAI, has drawn attention from global financial regulators. The Financial Stability Board (FSB) emphasizes the need for strong safeguards to mitigate AI risks.
